key_insight: The paper shows that two-qubit concurrence and three-qubit 3-tangle can be measured directly by mapping them to output probabilities in quantum circuits using unitary transformations and ancilla qubits.
engineering_relevance: This enables practical entanglement characterization on quantum hardware without full state tomography, reducing measurement overhead for quantum communication and quantum computing experiments.
method: Add auxiliary qubits to the target state.
Apply specific controlled unitary transformations that encode entanglement formulas into measurable probabilities.
Read out ancilla/output measurement probabilities to compute concurrence or 3-tangle directly.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a circuit-based scheme that analytically maps the bipartite concurrence and tripartite 3-tangle onto measurable output probabilities, avoiding full tomography.
watch_item: The approach is presented for pure two-qubit and three-qubit states, so extending it to noisy, mixed, or larger-scale systems may require additional circuit complexity and calibration.
paper_title: Entanglement Detection for Two-Qubit and Three-Qubit Pure States via Unitary Transformations and Ancilla State Measurements
